Norma was born June 11, 1947, and grew up in Brazil, where in her early teen years she worked as a busgirl and hostess at her family’s popular restaurant, Hunts’ Pleasant Acres. After graduating from Van Buren High School, she attended the University of Illinois Chicago. She married Frank Murphy and moved to Canada before eventually returning to Indiana, where she began her career with Hallmark. During her years with Hallmark, she managed and oversaw numerous stores throughout Indianapolis and the surrounding communities. Following her time with Hallmark, she continued her career in public service, working for the State of Indiana in Medicaid Policy. Norma found joy in many things, especially spending time with her family, caring for her cats and creating beautiful hand-knit items. Her knitting became more than a hobby, and she sold her work in several local boutiques. She also generously donated her handmade creations to orphanages and veterans organizations, taking great joy in using her talents to bless others. Throughout her life, Norma was involved in her community and church. She taught both children’s and adult Sunday School classes, served as PTA President, led Girl Scout troops, taught adult knitting classes, organized a knitting guild and was a proud member of the Daughters of the American Revolution. Norma is survived by her daughter, Julie Ann Milks (Ray); grandsons Nathan, Shawn and Damien; her brother, Norman J. Hunt, Jr. (Hiroko); her nephew, Chip Hunt; and her sister-in-law, Lynn Murphy. She was preceded in death by her first husband, Frank Murphy, and her parents, Geneva Rosemary (Schopmeyer) Hunt and Norman Jerome Hunt. A private graveside service will be held at Zion United Church of Christ Cemetery in Poland. A Celebration of Life will be held in Indianapolis at a later date. http://www.bignewsnetwork.com/news/27940.text: Big News Network.com 1st LD Writethru: Latvia's new parliament elects Edvards Smiltens as speaker RIGA, Nov. 3 (Xinhua) -- Latvia's 15th Saeima, or parliament, convened for its inaugural session on Tuesday and elected Edvards Smiltens of the United List as its speaker, marking his second term in the position. A total of 79 lawmakers voted in favor of Smiltens, while 15 voted against his appointment. Latvia held its parliamentary elections on Oct. 3, with the Central Election Commission announcing the final results on Oct. 16. The United List emerged as the largest political force, securing 41 of the 100 seats. Latvia First came second with 17 seats, followed by Sovereign Power/Alliance of Young Latvians with 15. The National Alliance and the Progressives each won 10 seats, while New Unity secured seven. Born in September 1984, Smiltens has served as both a member and deputy speaker of parliament. He previously held the position of parliamentary speaker from November 2022 to September 2023. Latvia has a unicameral parliament comprising 100 members elected for four-year terms. Under the Latvian Constitution, a newly elected parliament must convene for its first session on the first Tuesday of November following parliamentary elections, marking the end of the previous parliament's term.
